source: Round-24 cold-reader hand-test on the T-05 i18n diff BEFORE the §D6 amendment. The cold-reader correctly emitted veto with two HIGH findings — task-body caveats (chip deferral, Spanish-stub convention) were invisible to it because they lived in task notes rather than cited design. This is the canonical case for the 'silent producer resolution' failure mode the cold-reader is designed to catch.

input.task_description: T-05 — i18n key scaffolding (incidents namespace, excluding chips per task body)
input.verify_line: useTranslation('common') resolves all the new keys with no missing-key console warnings.
input.diff_summary: Adds incidents namespace to en/es common.json. Excludes incidents.chips.* (deferred to T-20). Spanish entries use English values as stubs (JSON disallows comments per task body). Adds incidents.i18n.test.ts asserting all keys resolve.

notes: Empirical proof the cold-reader catches the 'silent producer resolution' pattern when task-body caveats aren't reflected in cited spec/design. Companion to `regression-T-05-V2-post-amendment-clean-diff` which captures the same diff post-§D6-amendment producing clean approve. Together: the pair demonstrates the full escalation→resolution loop through the cold-reader/arbiter pipeline. Methodology finding: the underlying root cause (task-body caveats invisible to cold-reader) is logged as PR-B/methodology material; either builder needs to require cited-artifact authorization for deferrals, or cold-reader input needs visibility into task notes.
